run.question: Application-gateway server is returning 502 errors in the app-101 namespace. Please investigate.

report.summary: The reported problem could not be tied to anything observable in this Run, and the two observability backends needed to measure gateway 502s were unreachable throughout. The target cluster (m0-otel-20260909, window 2026-11-20T07:05:37Z to 2026-11-21T07:05:37Z) contains namespaces default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo; none is named app-101. Across the 29 Services and 24 Deployments returned, only one is gateway-facing: Service frontend-proxy (NodePort 30080) in otel-demo, with Deployment frontend-proxy 1/1 ready and available, pod frontend-proxy-844799bcdb-pv5mn Running and container-ready on the declared image, populated Service endpoints, a Ready single node with no pressure, and every flagd fault-injection flag in ConfigMap flagd-config set to defaultVariant 'off'. Countervailing detail: the frontend-proxy container declares no readiness or liveness probe, so its Ready state and endpoint membership do not demonstrate successful request handling. All Prometheus and Jaeger calls returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE and all pod log reads returned zero bytes, so gateway error rates, traces and log lines remain unknown rather than zero; accordingly no root cause is named.

claims.text: The namespaces returned for this cluster are default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo; no namespace named app-101 is among them.

Among the 29 Services returned across all namespaces, the only gateway-facing Service is frontend-proxy in otel-demo (type NodePort, port 8080, nodePort 30080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=frontend-proxy); no Service named application-gateway appears, and the other namespaces hold only kubernetes, kube-dns and metrics-server Services.
The Deployment list (24 objects, 21 of them in otel-demo plus coredns, metrics-server and local-path-provisioner) contains no Deployment named application-gateway or living in an app-101 namespace.
All 21 Deployments in otel-demo report ready=1 and available=1 with unavailable null, including frontend-proxy and frontend.

All 22 pods in otel-demo are in phase Running with every container reporting ready=true, including frontend-proxy-844799bcdb-pv5mn and frontend-6c9bc688bf-58jmw; none has a waiting state and no last termination reason is OOMKilled or Evicted.

Pod frontend-proxy-844799bcdb-pv5mn runs ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-frontend-proxy with imageID sha256:9cc478aa226b33cd80af46971683bfa963283a4309adf36d39706a406641ac7e, matching the image declared by Deployment frontend-proxy, whose only ReplicaSet is frontend-proxy-844799bcdb (desired 1, ready 1).

The frontend-proxy container spec in Deployment frontend-proxy declares no readinessProbe and no livenessProbe (env, containerPort 8080 and a 65Mi memory limit only), so its Ready condition and its presence in Service frontend-proxy endpoints do not demonstrate that it serves requests successfully.
Endpoints are populated for Service frontend (10.244.0.19:8080) and Service frontend-proxy (10.244.0.13:8080), and all 26 Endpoints objects in otel-demo list at least one address and port.

ConfigMap flagd-config in otel-demo declares 11 injection flags (productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad) and every one has defaultVariant 'off'.
The only node, opspilot-m1-control-plane, reports Ready=True with MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False and PIDPressure=False, with 8 CPU and 32859944Ki allocatable memory.

In otel-demo, pod prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn (container nginx) shows restartCount 3 with lastState.terminated.reason Error and exitCode 1, and kube-state-metrics-7cbf5b996-df4sz shows restartCount 2 with reason Error and exitCode 1, while the other otel-demo pods show restartCount 1 with reason Unknown and exitCode 255.

Pods in kube-system show the same restart pattern as otel-demo (coredns, kindnet-cni, kube-controller-manager, kube-proxy and kube-scheduler each restartCount 1 with lastState.terminated.reason Unknown and exitCode 255; metrics-server restartCount 2 with reason Error and exitCode 2), so the restartCount 1 / exit 255 pattern is not specific to the gateway workload.

The alerting_rules.yml held in ConfigMap prometheus in otel-demo contains only the opspilot-lab alert CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh (over traces_span_metrics_calls_total for service_name=checkout with span_name matching .*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder) and the opspilot-self alerts OpsPilotAgentAbsent and OpsPilotModelCallsFailing; no application-gateway or 502 alert rule appears in that file.

ConfigMap prometheus-readonly-proxy's container is nginx:1.28.0-alpine with a tcpSocket liveness and readiness probe on port 8080 and a configuration volume mounted at /etc/opspilot-proxy, and its pod has restarted 3 times with the last termination reason Error.

Pod-level failure of the gateway candidate is not observed: Deployment frontend-proxy reports 1 ready / 1 available and pod frontend-proxy-844799bcdb-pv5mn is Running with container ready=true, which argues against a crashed or evicted gateway pod as the source of the reported 502s.
Node-level resource pressure is not visible: the single node is Ready=True with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure all False.

A flagd fault-injection flag (for example adFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable or productCatalogFailure) causing the reported gateway 502s was considered and rejected: every flag in flagd-config has defaultVariant 'off', so no fault is switched on in that ConfigMap.

Service or endpoint misconfiguration behind the gateway was considered and is not supported for frontend-proxy: the frontend and frontend-proxy Services both have populated endpoint addresses, and the gateway Service port 8080 maps to containerPort 8080.

The reported 'application-gateway server' may correspond to otel-demo's frontend-proxy (Envoy, NodePort 30080) rather than to a literally named application-gateway in app-101, because frontend-proxy is the only gateway-facing Service in this cluster; this mapping is unconfirmed.

The repeated restarts of prometheus-readonly-proxy (nginx, restartCount 3, last termination reason Error, exit 1) are a possible reason the Prometheus source was unavailable to this Run, since Service prometheus-readonly-proxy (NodePort 30090 to targetPort 8080) is the only externally exposed Prometheus path in the cluster; the tooling's actual route is unknown and no causal link is established.

The last termination of the frontend-proxy container (reason Unknown, exit code 255) is more consistent with a cluster-wide container-runtime or node restart than with an application crash, because the same restartCount 1 / reason Unknown / exit 255 value appears on every otel-demo pod and on kube-system pods; this is unconfirmed.

Confirm with the alert source which cluster, target and namespace the 'application-gateway 502 in app-101' alert belongs to; app-101 does not exist on target m0-otel-20260909 and no workload named application-gateway is present there.

If frontend-proxy is the intended gateway, quantify 502s once metrics are reachable using traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy"} split by status_code and http_server_request_duration_seconds_count by status code, read the Envoy access/upstream-reset log lines, and add a readinessProbe to the frontend-proxy container so its Ready state reflects serving ability.

Inspect the prometheus-readonly-proxy nginx configuration and its restart cause (restartCount 3, last reason Error, exit 1) so the metrics path used for triage is reliable again; the configuration volume's source object is not in the readable ConfigMap list.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable for every call in this Run: get_all_labels, get_metric_names, get_series, get_prometheus_target, execute_prometheus_instant_query and metrics_range_query all returned status error with reason SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. No series could be read for gateway error rates, 5xx/502 counts (traces_span_metrics_calls_total by status_code, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count) or kube-state-metrics; those series are unknown, not zero.

Jaeger was unreachable for every call: traces_search, traces_list_operations and traces_list_services all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span-level evidence of gateway errors or upstream calls exists in this Run.

Application logs are unavailable: fetch_pod_logs returned status no_data with 0 lines and 0 bytes for both current and previous container instances of frontend-proxy-844799bcdb-pv5mn, frontend-6c9bc688bf-58jmw and prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn, so whether any 502 line was logged is unknown rather than absent.

The pod query for a 'gateway'/'101'-named or namespaced object returned status no_data with 0 matches over 32 pods, and the app-101 namespace and deployment queries likewise returned no_data; an empty result shows only that those queries matched nothing, so the absence of such pods cannot be cited as a positive finding.

The runbook's log step (kubectl logs ... | grep -i error) and its in-pod configuration check (kubectl exec ... appg -t) could not be carried out: log reads returned nothing and no pod-exec capability is among this Run's tools.
Events returned no_data: the all-namespace event query over the authorized window processed 0 events, so OOM, eviction and rollout evidence from events can be neither confirmed nor excluded.
The networkpolicies, resourcequotas and ingresses queries all returned no_data (0 objects), so neither the presence nor the absence of such objects can be asserted.

It is unknown what caused the cluster-wide restartCount 1 / reason Unknown / exit 255 pattern or when those terminations occurred; pod creation timestamps around 2026-11-20T16:32Z fall inside the authorized window, but current objects cannot prove earlier state.

The nginx configuration of prometheus-readonly-proxy is mounted from a configuration volume whose source object is not in the readable ConfigMap list and secrets cannot be read, so that configuration could not be verified.

Whether the reported alert originated from a different cluster or target, and whether any change was applied to this environment, is unknown: the change_history integration is not integrated in this Run.
next_steps: Ask the alerting party for the exact cluster, target and namespace behind the 'application-gateway 502 in app-101' alert, and re-run against that target if it is not m0-otel-20260909.

Restore or verify the Prometheus and Jaeger endpoints used by the tooling (including prometheus-readonly-proxy on NodePort 30090 and jaeger-query-nodeport on 30686), then re-evaluate gateway error metrics and traces.
If frontend-proxy is confirmed as the gateway in question, capture Envoy access logs with response code 502 and upstream reset details to identify which upstream cluster fails.
Review the prometheus-readonly-proxy and kube-state-metrics restart causes (last termination reason Error, exit codes 1 and 1), since they degrade the observability path used for this triage.

content:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
